findings.ac: A gate running `git merge-base $NW_BASE HEAD` on the worker succeeds and prints the same sha it prints in the coordinator's worktree
findings.title: `origin/<rest>` base name path (refs/remotes/origin/*) untested
findings.detail: The design also creates `refs/remotes/origin/<rest>` when `base.name` is `origin/<rest>` (`_checkout`, `name.startswith("origin/")`), and a coordinator whose `repo.base` is `origin/main` depends on it. Every test uses `base.name: "main"`. If that branch were removed or got the prefix wrong, `git rev-parse origin/main` / `{base}` would not resolve the way it does locally, and no test would fail. Add a merge-base/rev-parse case with `base: {name: "origin/main", sha}`.

findings.title: Gate deadline (slot hold + payload.gate_budget_s) and its fallback are not exercised
findings.detail: No test sends a small `payload.gate_budget_s` to check that a long gate is cut at slot-hold + budget, or that the budget falls back to the worker's `gate_budget_s` when it is absent. Wiring a wrong `deadline` (for example, measured from the claim time, or ignored) would go unnoticed. The cut itself is reused `run_gate_with_retries` code, which lowers the risk.

findings.title: Worker-provided gate env keys NW_DATA_DIR/NW_CONFIG_DIR/TMPDIR-per-job not asserted
findings.detail: The pass test checks `NW_WORKTREE`, and the retry test uses `$TMPDIR` implicitly, but nothing asserts that `NW_DATA_DIR`/`NW_CONFIG_DIR` are the worker's own or that `TMPDIR` is under `jobs/<id>/tmp`.

findings.title: `have` edge cases: missing cache returns [] and last-used refresh
findings.detail: `have` against a repo_key with no cache, and the claim that `have` refreshes `refs/nw/have/<sha>` and its last-used time (so a reported sha survives gc), are not directly tested.

findings.title: SIGHUP not covered
findings.detail: SIGTERM and SIGINT are parametrized mid-gate. SIGHUP, which is part of `_STOP_SIGNALS` and the most likely signal when the SSH session drops, is not.

findings.title: Unidentified one-off failure in the targeted set
findings.detail: The loop 6 test record notes one failure in 43 runs that was never identified. The suite is subprocess-heavy and concurrency-heavy (concurrent jobs, slot waits, signals). The tests use `until()` waits rather than sleeps, which is good, but the flake remains a residual risk.

findings.ac: `docs/WORKFLOW.md` documents the mandatory dedicated user and the absolute-path key line
findings.title: Docs AC is manual-only
findings.detail: The test plan makes this a manual check. The section is present in the diff. A small docs test that greps for the key line would keep it from regressing.
